correctness.rationale: Under the exact design assumptions, NN^T=(r-1)I+J. The explicit potentials x=(k/v)e_p-(1/v)1_B and y=(N^Tx-e_B)/k solve the grounded Poisson equation for unit injection on the incident edge. Their gradients give unique electrical flow. Every edge-avoiding route has length at least five; there are exactly (v-k)(k-1) five-edge bypasses and their uniform weights 1/(kv) reproduce the entire edge-current table. Positivity and path conservation then prove the two exact operator norms, dominance cases, and sharp bounds. A dependency-free exact rational checker independently confirmed 279 columns and 14064 bypass-path terms; finite checks are corroborative, not the infinite-family proof.

Generalized quadrangles have noncollinear point pairs, unlike an S(2,k,v); their incidence norm formula does not cover Steiner affine-plane graphs.

value.rationale: The unit electrical flow for every point-block edge in every Steiner pair design is a convex mixture supported only on shortest possible bypasses with universal equal weights, a nontrivial energy-versus-path-length rigidity independent of design isomorphism or edge transitivity. This supplies natural exact Banach-space endpoint invariants on infinitely many nonsymmetric affine and Steiner families, a complete cut/cycle dominance law, and optimal global bounds; the result is not an arbitrary finite sample or a reparameterization of only the symmetric case.
